issues.failure_explanation: For the same mode subset K, the C-term s^{|K|+1}C×_K[U̇ 0]… and the G-term s^{|K|}G×_K U̇… lie in the same subspace and are not orthogonal. The squared norm therefore contains cross terms that the expansion omits. In addition, the s^4 coefficient includes d(d-1) G-terms, each bounded by ||V||^4/σ^2, which the claimed bound binom(d,1)/σ^2 does not count. For example, d=3 and σ^2=3 require at least 3, but (1+1/σ^2)^3≈2.37. The stated c(X) is not proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound the error by the triangle inequality over subsets K and inflate c(X), for instance by a factor of 2^d·d. Propagate the new constant into ã and ā.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constants ã and ā in the stepsize lower bound and the sufficient-decrease constants are unreliable as stated.
issues.title: Curvature constant c(X) not established: expansion drops cross terms and undercounts terms
issues.why_classification: Only a constant changes. The O(s^2) structure and every qualitative conclusion survive.

issues.failure_explanation: prop: backtracking GRAP needs the Lipschitz constant on a ball of radius (√d+1)s̄||V_X||, because HOSVD iterates can lie that far from X. The proof instead uses radius √(d+1)s̄||V_X||, which is strictly smaller, and builds ε̄ from it. The inclusion of the required ball in B[X̲,ε̄] is therefore not shown.

failure_location.quote: We adopt~\cref{eq: Armijo GRAP} to $\tensX\in B[\underline{\tensX},\varepsilon_1(\underline{\tensX})]\cap\tensM_{\leq\vecr}$ and closed ball $B[\tensX,\sqrt{d+1}\bar{s}\|\tensV_\tensX\|_\frob]$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace √(d+1) by √d+1 in the ball and in ε̄. The inclusion then follows from the same estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform stepsize lower bound in the GRAP-R sufficient-decrease argument is not justified as written.
issues.title: Armijo result applied with a ball smaller than the one it requires
issues.why_classification: A constant correction that leaves the argument and its conclusions intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exists (at least) one non-negative term

issues.failure_explanation: The pointwise case split yields only ||V||^2 ≥ ½min{A,B}. At a non-stationary X̲, one of A or B can be zero. For instance, if ∇f(X̲)=e⊗u2⊗u3 with e⊥U1 and I={1}, then A>0 while B can be 0. Then δ̄=0 and δ(X̲)=0, which contradicts the claim δ>0. The argument also never links positivity to non-stationarity of X̲.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use bounds valid at every point: ||V_X||^2 ≥ c_I||∇f×_{k∉I}P_{U_k}||^2 and ||V_X||^2 ≥ Σ_{k∉I}||P^⊥_{U_k}(…)G^†G||^2. Both are continuous on the stratum, and by the normal-cone characterization their max is positive at a non-stationary X̲. Take δ̄ as half that max.
issues.overall_effect: Sufficient decrease near points of mixed Tucker rank is not established, so the apocalypse-freeness of GRAP-R is unproved for exactly these points.
issues.title: Case 3 lower bound uses a min of two quantities that can vanish at non-stationary points
issues.why_classification: The key lower-bound step must be replaced by a new contained argument tied to the normal-cone result, while the method and the theorem survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: it holds that $\underline{r}\leq \rank(\matx)$ for all $\matx\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $\|\matx-\underline{\matx}\|_\frob<\sigma_{\min}(\underline{\matx})$

issues.failure_explanation: prop: rank delta guarantees rank(X_(k)) ≥ r̲_k only when ||X−X̲|| < σ_min(X̲_(k)), but ε(X̲) imposes no such bound. Without it, X may lose rank in a mode k∉I. Then the candidate r̆ with r̆_k=r_k fails r̆ ≤ rank_tc(X) and need not lie in I_1×…×I_d.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add σ_min(X̲)/(2(√d+1)) to the min defining ε(X̲), as is done in prop: GRAP-R decrease.
issues.overall_effect: The admissibility of the chosen candidate, and hence the decrease bound in Case 2, is not guaranteed.
issues.title: rfGRAP-R neighborhood lacks the σ_min term needed for rank preservation in full-rank modes
issues.why_classification: A local addition of a standard condition with no change to the conclusions.

issues.failure_explanation: For k∈I, r̆_k may exceed r̲_k, so X_r̆ lies on a different stratum. P_{Ŭ_k} and the row spaces of its unfoldings do not converge to those of X̲, and the claimed bound ||P̃_k(∇f(X_r̆))|| ≥ ½||…(X̲)|| is unjustified. Likewise, the angle constant at X_r̆ involves r_k−r̆_k, which can be smaller than r_k−r̲_k, so using c_I(X̲) is not justified. The combined bound in terms of ||V̂_X̲|| therefore rests on unproved inequalities.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use only modes k∉I, where the mode ranks agree and continuity holds. Replace c_I by Π_{k∈I}1/min{n_k,n_{-k}}. Bound ||V_X̲||^2 by (1+|I|)||∇f×_{k∉I}P||^2 plus the k∉I tangent terms, as in the GRAP angle proof, to obtain a positive δ.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform positive δ(X̲) for rank-deficient X̲ in rfGRAP-R is not established, so its apocalypse-freeness is unproved.
issues.title: Lower bound on ||V_{X_r̆}|| claimed by continuity across strata of different mode ranks
issues.why_classification: The key lower bound must be re-derived with a modified, contained argument and new constants, while the theorem itself survives.
